title: Tragedy of the Commons Agent-Based Simulation
description: Add cows to a shared pasture and find the herd size at which the grass stops recovering between grazing cycles.
creator: Systems Thinking in the Age of AI
author: Dan McCreary
subject: Systems Thinking in the Age of AI
Tragedy of the Commons and Success to the Successful
chapter_title: Tragedy of the Commons and Success to the Successful

educational.learningObjective: Given control over the size of a shared herd, the learner will identify the herd size at which the pasture stops recovering between grazing cycles.
prerequisites: Knows what a shared resource is
learningOutcomes: Identify the threshold herd size at which a commons stops recovering
Explain why individually rational choices produce a collectively irrational outcome
Recognize that past the threshold the cost falls on everyone, not just the last entrant
educational.assessmentOpportunity: Ask learners to state the threshold they found and to explain why no individual herder has a reason to stop below it.

pedagogical.interactionPattern: Parameter-sweep agent simulation with a threshold to discover
pedagogical.instructionalStrategy: Guided discovery of a critical threshold
pedagogical.feedbackType: Live grass regrowth and cow health as the herd grazes
misconceptionsAddressed: That only the extra animals suffer once capacity is exceeded
That the collapse requires someone to behave badly
discussionQuestions: Why does dividing the pasture into private plots change the outcome?
What are the commons in your organization - meeting time, shared databases, on-call capacity?
Elinor Ostrom found real communities that avoid this collapse. What do they have that this simulation does not?
